facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal of the eGabon project sets the baseline for health workers who regularly use and update the patient's electronic medical record during consultations at 0 per cent in 2016, with yearly targets rising to 20, 45 and 70 per cent; the national system holding that record was still to be designed, built and rolled out, first in one region and then nationwide.
facts.system: National Health Information System (NHIS) electronic medical record

facts.fact: The 2016 World Bank appraisal states that the health ministry (MSPSSN) and the state digital agency ANINF are to develop and roll out the National Health Information System, including a standardised electronic medical record on a common patient identifier, with a National Health Information Center to be set up.
facts.system: National Health Information System (NHIS) electronic medical record

facts.fact: The 2016 World Bank appraisal costs the National Health Information System component at US$41.58 million, of which US$40.08 million is an IBRD loan and US$1.50 million government counterpart funding, the counterpart to cover a rising share of operating costs (0, 25 and 50 per cent in years 3 to 5).
facts.system: National Health Information System (NHIS) electronic medical record

systems.platform: to be designed; open source applications to be used where feasible
systems.owner: MSPSSN (health ministry) and ANINF, financed by the World Bank eGabon project (P132824)
systems.tiers: planned for all facilities, public, private, military and prison, after a first region; not yet in use in 2016
some hospitals; a limited number of electronic systems exist, largely independent and not exchanging data

note: Passages file of an appraisal document: everything about the NHIS is a plan as of May 2016, not a deployment. The planned NHIS also includes a data warehouse and reporting for decision-making, which the passages do not describe closely enough to take an hmis fact. The document counts about 130 health centres and almost 600 health posts and dispensaries, a possible denominator for primary clinics.
